newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Europe's big companies asked to help the small ones.
newsitem.headline: Europe's big companies asked to help the small ones.

text.p: Europe could boost its sagging ability to compete in global markets if big companies worked more closely with small ones, a report published by a group of top European corporations said on Monday.

"Partnerships between large and small companies have become a central feature of the business world," Morris Tabaksblat, chairman and CEO of Anglo-Dutch conglomerate Unilever Plc, said in a statement.
"Europe is losing out in comparison to its competitors," he added. "It is not modernising its industrial and economic structures quickly enough."

The report, published by the European Round Table of Industrialists, found that small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) that received support from large companies had an 80 percent survival rate after five years -- compared with the 50 percent European average.
It said big operators could help, for example, by engaging in "positive restructuring" -- spinning off units to SMEs rather than closing them down completely.
They could also share training resources or offer start-up grants or unsecured loans to small companies.
Governments could help by easing up on the regulatory burdens that hamper SMEs, "one of Europe's major competitive handicaps", it added.

"Greater innovation and its more rapid introduction will do much to create new jobs," the statement said. It called for science parks and technology clusters that bring together large and small companies, university researchers, technical advisers and venture capitalists.
The European Round Table groups the chairmen of 45 leading European companies.
